header.running_head: The Hijrah of Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA)

blocks.text: With special reference to him, the following verse of the Qur'aan was revealed:

blocks.arabic_text: وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا
blocks.text: Whoever leaves his home to make Hijrah towards (a place where he can fulfil the commands of) Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ and then death finds him (en route), without doubt his reward is assured (set aside) by Allaah. Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. [^1]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Dhamra bin Jundub (RA) left his house to make Hijrah, he told his family members, "Put me on my mount. Remove me from the land of the Mushrikeen and take me to Rasulullaah ﷺ." However, he passed away en route before reaching Rasulullaah ﷺ. It was then that the following verse of the Qur'aan was revealed:

Whoever leaves his home to make Hijrah towards (a place where he can fulfil the commands of) Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ and then death finds him (en route), without doubt his reward is assured (set aside) by Allaah. Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. [^2]
The Hijrah of Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA)

Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) narrates that he left home with the intention of accepting Islaam and came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Since Rasulullaah ﷺ was leading the salaah at the time, he joined the rows at back and performed salaah with the Sahabah (RA). After completing the salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ went to Hadhrat Waathila (RA) at the back and asked him what it was that he wanted. When he replied that he intended accepting Islaam, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "That is best for you." Rasulullaah ﷺ then asked him whether he intended making Hijrah. When he replied in the affirmative, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Will it be a Hijrah Baadi or a Hijrah Baati?" "Which is better?" asked Hadhrat Waathila (RA). "The Hijrah Baati," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then went on to explain, "The Hijrah Baati is that you live with Rasulullaah ﷺ (in Madinah) while the Hijrah Baadi is that you return to your locality. (In any event) You will be required to obey (my commands and the commands of Allaah) in conditions of ease and adversity, whether you are willing or not and even though others are given preference over you." After Hadhrat Waathila (RA) had agreed, Rasulullaah ﷺ stretched out his hand and Hadhrat Waathila (RA) stretched out his hand (to pledged allegiance). When Rasulullaah ﷺ saw that Hadhrat Waathila (RA) was not going to make any exceptions to the pledge, Rasulullaah ﷺ prompted him to add, "As far as I am able."
